text:
**Yes, but only some models can, and a basic power station may let your computer reboot during an outage.**

**What to look for**
- **Documented UPS/EPS mode with automatic switchover.** Anker says a power station can work as a UPS only with documented UPS or EPS functionality, a suitable transfer time, and enough output and battery capacity. A basic one may keep appliances running but still interrupt a computer. ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups))
- **Transfer time of about 10 ms or less.** EcoFlow warns that many products advertised as UPS take 20-30 ms to switch, which it says can cause data loss. ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)) Anker is more measured: 10 or 20 ms may be fine for some devices, but it isn't 0 ms, so check your device's manual. ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas))
- **Pure sine wave output** and **enough continuous wattage** for your PC and monitor combined.
- **Pass-through support.** Charging while powering a load is not the same as UPS protection. Confirm the model's UPS section in its manual.

**Models from the results**
- [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups): 2,010Wh, 1,500W pure sine wave output, and a 10 ms UPS switchover. It was listed at $699.99 after coupon.
- [EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply): under 10 ms switchover and 600W AC output, which EcoFlow says is enough for a desktop and external drives. The page gave no price. EcoFlow also lists the DELTA Pro 3 as a UPS, but the article says ">10ms", which is probably a typo. Verify that figure before buying.
- **EcoFlow DELTA 3 series:** the support pages have an FAQ on UPS status and switching time, but the answers weren't in the results, so check them first. ([DELTA 3 Classic](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/delta-3-classic-portable-power-station/support))
- **Bluetti:** the pricing page I found lists models like the [AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) ($499) but gives no UPS or switchover specs, so I can't say whether they suit this. Check Bluetti's spec sheet first. That page is an affiliate site, so treat its links accordingly.

**Caveats**
- These are manufacturers' blogs, so they have a sales interest.
- For critical data or servers, an online double-conversion UPS (0 ms transfer) is the safer choice.
- Before buying, check your PC's power draw with a plug-in watt meter. Then test by pulling the wall plug while the PC is running.
- Runtime is roughly Wh × 0.85 ÷ watts. A 2,010Wh unit running a 150W desktop would last about 11 hours in ideal conditions.

If you tell me your PC's wattage and whether you need hours of runtime or just a safe shutdown, I can narrow this down. For a safe shutdown only, a regular UPS is usually cheaper.
